sentences.text: On 15 October, the government announced more than £41 million to help repair old buildings in England.
sentences.zh: 10月15日，政府宣布提供超过4,100万英镑，帮助修缮英格兰的老建筑。

sentences.text: The support will reach 74 places, including churches, town halls and castles.
sentences.zh: 这笔支持将惠及74处地点，包括教堂、市政厅和城堡。

sentences.text: These buildings are part of local history, but some need important repairs before people can use them again.
sentences.zh: 这些建筑是当地历史的一部分，但有些需要进行重要修缮，人们才能重新使用。

sentences.text: In Margate, the museum and old town hall will receive money for work on the buildings.
sentences.zh: 在马盖特，博物馆和旧市政厅将获得用于建筑工程的资金。

sentences.text: The museum plans to protect its collections better and make visits easier for the public.
sentences.zh: 博物馆计划更好地保护馆藏，让公众参观更加方便。

sentences.text: The empty town hall will become a place with several different uses for the community.
sentences.zh: 闲置的市政厅将成为供社区多种用途使用的场所。

sentences.text: In Blackpool, money will help with the first stage of work on a former post office.
sentences.zh: 在布莱克浦，资金将帮助开展一座旧邮局的第一阶段工程。

sentences.text: The plan is to turn it into a cultural and creative centre led by the community.
sentences.zh: 计划是将其改造成由社区主导的文化创意中心。

sentences.text: This first stage will make the building's structure secure and move plans forward.
sentences.zh: 这一阶段将加固建筑结构并推进相关计划。

sentences.text: The announcement describes future work; it does not say that all these buildings are already open.
sentences.zh: 公告描述的是未来工程，并没有说这些建筑都已开放。

sentences.note: turn ... into ... 表示把某物改造成另一种用途；it指上一句的旧邮局，led by the community说明由社区主导。

questions.text: Which part of this story matters most to everyday life, and why?
questions.zh: 这则报道的哪一部分与日常生活最相关？为什么？
